subject: Question: ML CFA with ordered categorical data

messages.author: 560bcf3647a0df9b
messages.subject: Question: ML CFA with ordered categorical data
parts:
Does anyone know if lavaan can run maximum likelihood estimates with ordered-categorical data under a CFA framework? 

If so how? I am under the impression that I can only do this with OpenMx, but I hope that is not the case.


Thanks!
Christi Phillips

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Question: ML CFA with ordered categorical data
parts:
Maximum likelihood estimation assumes (conditional) multivariate normality, but ordered categorical data are not normally distributed. So using ML estimation would mean that you were assuming the data were not ordered categorical.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Question: ML CFA with ordered categorical data
parts:
If you choose MLR estimation, then you are treating the observed values as if they are actual numbers, not just ordered labels ("Never" "Sometimes" "Always"), as they are if the data are only ordinal. You can't use MLR with ordinal data. You either treat the data as ordinal and don't use MLR, or you treat the data as continuous but nonnormal and use MLR or some other continuous data estimator.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Question: ML CFA with ordered categorical data
parts: I've had the same problem. In Mplus you can run the robust maximum likelihood estimator with ordered data...but not yet in R.

I addressed your misunderstanding in your other thread:  https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/LunOL4ZctV4/Mb7z0JqgAAAJ

Short answer: MLR is not available in Mplus for ordinal data, that is just a misleading keyword they use to trigger MML estimation, which IS available in R (lavaan, mirt, other IRT packages).  When using the probit link, they all assume a normally distributed latent item response underlying ordinal observations, and there is no robust option to free us from that assumption with moving to Bayesian MCMC estimation.

Also in response to the last person's comment, here is a helpful article justifying and supporting the use of MLR estimator with ordinal data:https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-015-0619-7

They were less supportive than you imply, but Rhemtulla et al. (2012) were more supportive and informative when they published almost the same study a few years prior.   The ordinal data should have at least 5 categories (when approximately normal) or at least 7 categories (if thresholds are asymmetric) to treat as continuous using MLR.
  
http://psychmodels.ucdavis.edu/uploads/8/6/3/9/86398102/rhemtullabrosseauliardsavalei_pm.pdf
